requests.prompt:
Create ONE polished landscape illustrated product-research board in English, panel 1 of a coordinated four-board series for Frank and Harry's Open Verified Autonomy pet robot exploration. Use case: infographic-diagram with rich editorial illustration, not a technical schematic. 3:2 landscape, large readable English typography, generous margins, warm ivory background, dark navy typography, teal and muted amber highlights. Sophisticated approachable industrial design presentation, clean isometric/soft 3D imagery. No logos or fabricated numbers.
Title exact: "01 / WHY A PET ROBOT?"
Subtitle exact: "A need worth exploring — not yet a validated product"
Main scene: cozy apartment, a normal orange-and-white domestic cat near a small rounded low mobile robot; an owner near doorway with a travel bag, indicating the long-term context, not proof of unattended readiness. Small research cards with exact text:
"OWNER NEED" / "Meaningful play when people are busy or away"
"CAT'S CHOICE" / "Approach, engage, pause or leave"
"DESIGN QUESTION" / "Will a cat voluntarily interact with a moving robot?"
Bottom three small visual hypothesis cards:
"Interest" / "Does the cat approach?"
"Comfort" / "Does it stay or withdraw?"
"Repeatability" / "Does interest return over several sessions?"
Bottom note exact: "Source: one owner's suggestion. Demand and cat response still need testing."
Do not imply cats universally enjoy robots. No medical claims, no market stats, no lasers, no strings, no food dispensers. Show robot stopped at a respectful distance, cat free to walk away. This is a conceptual needs board, not marketing claims. All text English, accurately spelled.

Create ONE polished landscape English visual storyboard, panel 2 of a coordinated four-board series for Frank and Harry's pet robot concept. Use case illustration-story/product interaction board. 3:2 landscape, warm ivory, navy typography, teal and muted amber highlights, clean high-end soft 3D/editorial illustration. Same visual protagonist throughout: orange-and-white domestic cat and small low rounded cream/teal mobile robot with protected wheels. Adult human supervisor visible in background or lower supervision strip. Large readable English typography, balanced white space.
Title exact: "02 / INVITE PLAY. DO NOT CHASE."
Subtitle exact: "First experiment: short, supervised interaction"
Four generously sized numbered storyboard panels in a 2x2 grid:
"1  OBSERVE" / "A person checks the space and the cat's response."
Show robot stopped, cat distant, human observing.
"2  INVITE" / "The operator makes one short, slow movement."
Show operator holding controller; robot moving a short distance away from cat, subtle short trajectory, no pursuit toward cat.
"3  PAUSE" / "Stop and let the cat choose whether to approach."
Show stationary robot, curious cat approaching voluntarily.
"4  END" / "Stop if the cat withdraws or the operator intervenes."
Show cat freely leaving and robot stationary with stop icon.
Bottom strip exact: "Log: approach • pursuit • withdrawal • operator stops"
Small footer exact: "Concept protocol — no unsupervised use or automatic emotion recognition assumed."
No aggressive chase, no trapped cat, no cables or strings, no laser. This board illustrates a proposed experiment, not tested capability.

Create ONE high-quality landscape English industrial-design concept board, panel 3 of four for Frank and Harry's pet-interaction robot. Use case product-mockup with explanatory illustrations. 3:2, high-end studio 3D renders on warm ivory, dark navy labels, teal and muted amber highlights. Readable uncluttered English, all functionality clearly conceptual, no claimed certified safety.
Title exact: "03 / PROTOTYPE NOW. PRODUCT LATER."
Subtitle exact: "Reuse mature hardware; test the interaction before redesigning it"
Two distinct zones, left 45%, right 55%, with a small arrow labeled "Learn before redesign".
LEFT heading exact: "LEARNING PROTOTYPE"
Render a small generic L150-like four-wheel laboratory mobile base: rectangular two-tier aluminum plates, four black rubber fixed wheels, controller board, battery, optional camera and lidar modules mounted securely. Not exact brand, no product logo. Include a controller held by a human hand nearby. Do not show a cat interacting with exposed prototype mechanics.
Three captions:
"Purchased chassis and supported computer"
"Vendor tutorials and recoverable software"
"Manual control and recorded observations"
Small label "Sensor package: confirm with supplier".
RIGHT heading exact: "FUTURE CONCEPT"
Hero render of compact low rounded cream/teal robot, softly covered shell, recessed camera, guarded wheel openings, reachable top stop button. Orange-and-white cat at respectful distance. Elegant thin callouts, not dimensioned mechanical drawings:
"Rounded enclosure"
"Protected wheel openings"
"Low camera viewpoint"
"Accessible stop control"
Small adjacent bottom card titled "TO VALIDATE" with exact text:
"Noise • fur entanglement • stability • cleaning • cat response"
Footer exact: "Concept design only. Protective features and animal suitability require testing."
No dimensions, no invented sensors performance, no cat riding robot, no robotic arms, no dangling toys, no laser, no claims of production readiness.

Create ONE polished English landscape illustrated roadmap board, panel 4 of a coordinated series for Frank and Harry's pet robot exploration. Use case productivity-visual / editorial roadmap, not precise engineering diagram. 3:2, warm ivory background, dark navy typography, teal and muted amber accents, soft isometric 3D vignettes with an orange-and-white cat, generic small four-wheel robot and desktop computer. Three illustrated sequential cards:
"REPRODUCE" / "Restore the vendor setup and run basic tutorials"
"UNDERSTAND" / "Explain sensors, commands and stopping"
"EXPERIMENT" / "Try supervised play and make one reversible change"

Middle review card exact heading "REVIEW BEFORE MOVING ON" with text:
"Can both teammates repeat the baseline, explain one change and investigate one failure?"
Lower amber-tinted area titled "STAGE 2 / RK3588 — LATER"

Use generic single-board computer illustration labelled RK3588; no invented benchmark values.
Bottom tiny team strip exact: "Frank: software + vision   |   Harry: integration + navigation   |   Both: experiments + cross-review"
Footer exact: "Tutorial reproduced ≠ capability verified. Unattended pet use remains future work."
No schedule promises, no approved procurement claim, no market validation claim. All English text.
